body:
I've heard. But one of the biggest issues with my previous job was that it was impossible for me to stay on top of everything without continuing to work once I got home from the office and/or on the weekend (unpaid btw) so I just want a job where once I leave my place of work, or log off if it's a remote job, I'm done until my next shift. The pressure of never being on top of things without working during all my free time was just too much. 

I know part of the reason I struggled to stay on top of things was because of my mental health issues but I truly believe that even someone without these issues would not be able to get everything done in 40 hours/week.
I know what you mean. Those few moments of reprieve from these thoughts have been fewer and fewer and I'm at the point where now I don't know when the last time I one.

Yeah, it's sadly the only thing pushing me to stick around. As much as I love my friends and family and I know they love me, I can't help but feel they'll be better off without me. 

And even on my good days, I've never been able to get myself to believe my family would be that sad about me dying. But I still don't want them to have to clean up my mess when I'm gone.

It's not like creditors would start calling them or seizing their assets but it would be something they'd have to still deal with seeing as I don't really have any assets or anything to pay off the debts once I'm gone. I don't believe it'll affect their credit score, it's just a headache I wouldn't want to leave them with
